summary: Build a playful Valentine’s Day “question” micro-app with a short multi-screen flow, cute theme, a dodging NO button gag, and celebratory YES outcome effects.
imageRequirements:
## Required Images
- Seamless cute heart pattern background in pink/red/soft-purple palette (valentine-pattern.dim_1600x900.png)
- Soft gradient background with subtle bokeh/hearts in pink/red/soft-purple palette (valentine-gradient-bg.dim_1600x900.png)
- Minimal rounded heart icon sticker style, soft purple/pink tones (heart-sticker-icon.dim_256x256.png)

existing_features.title: Implement a 4-step, single-page Valentine micro-app flow with clearly separated screens: (1) Intro screen, (2) Build-up screen, (3) Big Question screen, (4) Sweet Ending screen. Navigation must be driven by button clicks and not require any backend calls.
Create the Intro screen with the exact user-facing text (in English) and a single primary button labeled “Continue”. Text must read: “Hi Anya 💕\nI made a tiny app just to ask you something…”
Create the Build-up screen with the exact user-facing text (in English) and a single primary button labeled “I’m ready”. Text must read: “This is a very serious question.\nPlease answer honestly 😌”

Create the Big Question screen with big, bold centered text: “Anya, will you be my Valentine? 💝”. Under it, render two buttons: “YES 💕” and “NO”. Render a small, subtle line of helper text under the buttons: “(Just kidding… but I really hope you say yes 🥺)”.

Implement the “dodging NO button” interaction on the Big Question screen: when the user attempts to click/tap the NO button (including pointer hover on desktop and touch/pointer down on mobile), the NO button must evade the pointer by moving (slide/jump) to a new position within a bounded area on the screen. The YES button must remain stationary and easy to click.

Show playful, non-pressuring feedback messages near the buttons when NO is dodged. Randomly pick from the provided list and display one at a time, briefly (auto-fade) after each dodge attempt. Messages (English, exactly): “Hey hey hey 😳”, “Nice try”, “That button is shy”, “Wrong choice detected 🚫”, “The universe says no… to NO”.

When the user clicks “YES 💕”, play a celebratory sequence: (1) confetti burst, (2) hearts raining animation, (3) a short vibration on supported devices (use browser vibration API if available). Then show the success message (English, exactly): “Best decision ever 🥰\nHappy Valentine’s Day, Anya ❤️” and the follow-up text: “Dinner / chocolate / cuddles are officially planned 😏”.

Add the Sweet Ending screen text (English, exactly): “I promise this app is the only thing that won’t let you say no 😉\nThank you for being you.” Provide a clear, gentle way to reach it after the YES celebration (automatic after a short delay or via a “Continue” button).

Apply the requested visual style across all screens: a cute Valentine theme using pink, red, and soft purple; rounded, friendly typography; gentle animations that are not overwhelming. Ensure the overall tone stays playful/cute and not pushy or uncomfortable (e.g., avoid shaming language and keep all microcopy light).
Add optional soft romantic background music with an on-screen mute/unmute control that defaults to muted or requires an explicit user action to start playback (to respect browser autoplay policies).
Add generated static visual assets and render them in the UI as part of the theme (served from frontend/public/assets/generated).

new_feature_requests.summary: Create Valentine micro-app with intro/build-up/question screens, dodging NO button behavior with playful messages, and YES celebration (confetti/hearts/vibration) plus optional sweet ending and romantic styling/music.
